en.title: Rotate Vowel Positions Right
en.description:
Cyclically shift the lowercase vowels a, e, i, o, u in the string one position to the right in order of appearance: each vowel moves to the position of the next vowel, and the last one moves to the position of the first. All other characters stay in place. If there are no vowels, output the string unchanged.

The input format, examples, and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: A single line of printable ASCII text of length 1..1000, which may contain spaces; only the lowercase aeiou count as vowels.
en.output: Output the answer as described; separate multiple results with spaces in order, and output an empty line for an empty array.
en.explanation: Example 1: the vowels of codesignal are o, e, i, a in order; after rotating right they become a, o, e, i, and writing them back into the original vowel positions gives cadosegnil. The output must keep all original spaces and end with a newline.
hints: Extract the vowels, rotate them right by one, then write them back into the original vowel positions in order.
